moat_against: Government payers set much of reimbursement; Medicare/Medicaid rates lag cost inflation and supplemental Medicaid benefits are set to shrink under OBBBA from 2028
Labor shortages (nurses, psychiatrists, techs) constrain capacity and drive wage/professional-fee costs
ROIC proxy only 7.2-12.9% over 2022-2025 — thin spread over cost of capital, volatile
Larger rivals (HCA in acute care, Acadia in behavioral) and non-profit systems compete for patients, physicians and staff in every local market
Professional/general liability severity rising — reserve increases in Q2 2026
moat_for: Largest US behavioral-health platform; inpatient psychiatric beds structurally undersupplied locally
Scale across ~400 facilities in acute care and behavioral health; negotiating leverage with commercial payers
Diversified acute + behavioral mix, resilient through cycles; operating margin recovered to 11.5% in FY2025
Local facility density, licensure/CON barriers and referral relationships in served markets
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow: local scale and scarce behavioral-health beds plus diversified acute/behavioral footprint, but payer-set reimbursement, labor scarcity and ROIC that fell to 7.2% in 2022 and only recovered to 12.9% in 2025 — not well above cost of capital through a cycle.
name: Universal Health Services, Inc.
one_liner: Solid hospital operator, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $185.10 (11.1% weighted IRR, IV@15% $125.26); clears 15% only below ~$125, with Medicaid supplemental cuts and leverage capping the upside.
sector: Healthcare / Hospitals — acute care and behavioral health
